narr: A deep, negatively tilted upper level trough and associated occluded front passed from the central Mississippi River Valley on January 9th toward the lower New England region by the morning of the 10th. Strong southerly wind flow ahead of the upper trough carried deep moisture from the Gulf of Mexico northward into the Carolinas and the lower Mid-Atlantic. Precipitable water values ranged from 1.1 inches across north-central Virginia to nearly 1.5 inches over the border between Virginia and North Carolina by early afternoon on the 9th, or anywhere between two and three standard deviations above normal for January. Precipitation fell mainly as rain during a 12 to 15 hour period on the 9th, mostly at rates of a half inch per hour or less. However, a convective band pushed from North Carolina across the foothills and Piedmont of southern Virginia during the afternoon, producing rates of locally two inches per hour. Rainfall totals varied from 1.5 to 2.5 inches for portions of Virginia located west of the Blue Ridge Parkway, and between 2.5 and 3.5 inches along and further east of the parkway, averaging between 2-year and 5-year precipitation totals for a 12 hour duration per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. Given that multiple precipitation events having passed across the region since late November 2023 had allowed stream flows and soil moisture to improve from the Moderate to Severe Drought conditions, the region was more susceptible to flooding. The long-duration rainfall event allowed streams to rise gradually, making for numerous instances of mainly minor areal and riverine flooding. However, flash flooding occurred across the Piedmont, particularly across Pittsylvania County, in the wake of the convective band. Multiple roads and bridges were reported flooded and impassible because of the rainfall, with a few becoming severely damaged.
ev: After around 1.75 inches of rain had fallen over a roughly 10 hour period, a line of heavy rainfall, producing rates of 1.5 inches per hour, passed across Pittsylvania County, bringing a half inch to three quarters of rain over a short period of time. This resulted in numerous instances of flash flooding throughout the county. Runoff from this rain caused Green Rock Branch to overflow its banks at least six inches deep across Concord Road. Motleys Mill Road washed out near the intersection with Halifax Road, causing an estimated 50 thousand dollars worth of damage. Halifax Road was also observed flooded. Sycamore Creek was observed overflowing its banks several inches deep across Country Club Road. Extensive damage occurred near the intersection of Walkers Well Road and Toshes Road, with three layers of the road surface washed away, causing an estimated 25 thousand dollars of damage. Long Branch Creek was observed overflowing its banks several inches deep across Player Road, leaving a large amount of debris on the roadway. Fall Creek rose several inches out of its banks, flooding the southbound lane of N. Main Street near Fall Creek Drive. Cascade Creek was observed out of its banks several inches deep over Cobbs Knob Road. Pudding Creek was observed overflowing its banks across Johnson Road, and across the Jones Mill Road bridge. White Ridge Road was submerged several inches deep as Barker Creek overflowed its banks. Cedar Creek was observed overflowing its banks at least several inches deep Graves Bridge Road. Little Bearskin Creek was reported out of its banks several inches deep over Hollywood Road. Anderson Mill Road was completely washed out and impassible near the intersection with Old Red Eye Road, causing an estimated 50 thousand dollars worth of damage. Both Countryside Drive and Hillside Drive was observed with several inches of water flowing across the roadway surface. Shawnee Road was observed flooded several inches deep between Sandy Bottom Road and Camp Shawnee Road. Green Rock Branch was observed flowing well outside of its banks. Both Berry Hill Road and Stateline Bridge Road were observed flooded several inches deep by flowing water. Fall Creek Road was observed flooded by nearby Cane Creek overflowing its banks. The 1000 block of Terry Road was reported flooded. The 2000 block of Irish Road was reported flooded and impassible. Strawberry Road was flooded and closed as the Banister River rose out of its banks.

After around 1.75 inches of rain had fallen over a roughly 10 hour period, a line of heavy rainfall, producing rates of 1.5 inches per hour, passed across Campbell County, bringing a half inch to three quarters of rain over a short period of time. This resulted in several instances of flash flooding across central Campbell County. Tussocky Creek was reported out of its banks, flowing across Depot Road near Lazy Creek Drive. Flowing water was observed several inches deep over the intersection of Willow Lake Way and Depot Road. Red House Road was observed completely flooded several inches deep as Jacobs Creek overflowed its banks. Sunnymeade Road was completely flooded several inches deep near the intersection with Candlers Mountain Road.
A creek (name unknown) overflowed its banks and partially washed out a bridge on Rockwood Park Drive.
